headline: BEST EVER: Aya Gold Hits 890 g/t AgEq Over 51.5m at Morocco's Boumadine — New Parallel Vein Found
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX:AYA) delivered its strongest-ever drill intercept at Boumadine, Morocco — 890 g/t silver equivalent over 51.5 metres just 70 metres below the current pit shell — while identifying a new high-grade parallel structure. With 11 rigs turning and a 69,000-metre year-to-date program underway, an updated PEA is due mid-2026.

headline: INFILL CONFIRMS GRADE: Freegold Drills 33.7 g/t Au Over 19.5m at Alaska's 17Moz Golden Summit
snippet: Freegold Ventures (TSX:FVL) released infill drill results from Alaska's Golden Summit — 33.7 g/t Au over 19.5m and 19.2 g/t Au over 24.7m — validating the high-grade corridors inside one of North America's largest undeveloped gold deposits (17.2Moz indicated, 11.9Moz inferred). The 50,000-metre program is accelerating toward a pre-feasibility study.

headline: NexGold Extends GOLDLUND Deposit With Broad Intercepts — 7.59 g/t Au Over 9m in Northwestern Ontario
snippet: NexGold Mining (TSX:NEXG) added another round of broad, high-grade intercepts at its Goldlund Deposit in northwestern Ontario — including 7.59 g/t Au over 9.0m and 3.31 g/t Au over 20.0m — reinforcing deposit continuity and expansion potential ahead of a planned mineral resource update.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,500: Still 36% Higher Year-Over-Year as Iran Tensions and 3.8% Inflation Cap the Rally
snippet: Gold traded at $4,503 per ounce on May 20, up 35.65% year-over-year but 19% below its January 2026 all-time high of $5,589. U.S. inflation running at 3.8% and Middle East conflict driving oil prices higher are stoking rate-hike expectations that are capping near-term upside, even as institutional year-end targets remain at $5,000-plus.

headline: COPPER AT $6.18/LB — Tariff Deadline and Mine Disruptions Push Metal 34% Higher Than a Year Ago
snippet: Copper rose to $6.18 per pound on May 20, up 33.69% year-over-year, as pre-positioning ahead of the U.S. June 30 copper tariff review combines with ongoing supply disruptions in Chile, Indonesia, and Peru. Goldman Sachs sees a 160,000-tonne surplus; the International Copper Study Group counters with a 150,000-tonne deficit — and the spread is keeping prices volatile.

headline: SIGMA LITHIUM Fights Brazil Court's "Fake" $10M Collateral Order — Ruling Dropped During Record Earnings Week
snippet: Sigma Lithium (NASDAQ:SGML) is appealing a May 17 local court ruling in Brazil's Vale do Jequitinhonha that could require a US$10 million collateral over alleged waste pile damage at its Grota do Cirilo lithium operation. The company says the decision is unwarranted and that a "fake news" campaign appeared in coordination with its record quarterly earnings.

headline: URANIUM AT $84.50/lb — META Signs 7.8 GW Nuclear Deal, MICROSOFT Locks In 800 MW, Forcing Supply Rethink
snippet: Uranium spot held at $84.50 per pound on May 20, up 18.93% year-over-year, as Big Tech's race to secure nuclear power for AI data centres — Meta (7.8 GW contracted), Microsoft (800 MW) — shifts the demand story from utilities alone to a structural floor bid. NexGen's Rook I in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin is set to begin construction this summer with 30 million lb/year capacity.

headline: CHINA RARE EARTH INDEX DROPS to 251.4 — Ex-China Terbium Still 3–5x Higher as the Bifurcation Widens
snippet: China's official rare earth price index fell to 251.4 on May 20 — with terbium oxide at $905–914/kg — as the domestic market consolidates after a 105% run since January's open. Outside China, heavy rare earth prices remain 3–5x higher due to limited non-Chinese separation capacity, with the structural gap widening even as the index corrects.

headline: China Bought 790+ Tons of Silver in Early 2026 — And Ghana's New GOLD ROYALTY Is Squeezing Miner Margins
snippet: This week's Gold SWOT highlights two under-covered mining stories: China's massive silver accumulation (790+ tonnes in early 2026, largely tied to solar panel manufacturing) and Ghana's new tiered royalty that can reach 12% when gold exceeds $4,500/oz — a rate now triggered almost daily that analysts say may redirect West African mining investment toward more royalty-friendly jurisdictions.

headline: J.P. Morgan, Goldman, BofA All Hold $5,000 GOLD Year-End Targets — Why Institutional Forecasters Won't Blink
snippet: Despite gold pulling back 19% from its $5,589 January all-time high, institutional forecasters are holding the line: J.P. Morgan at $5,055 by Q4 2026, Goldman Sachs at $4,900, Bank of America at $5,000. The bullish case rests on central banks buying 244 tonnes in Q1, persistent real-rate suppression, and six years of structural supply underinvestment.

headline: Silver Up 150% in a Year — But STOP CHASING the Number: Why $84 Is Not the Entry Point
snippet: Silver surged from under $34 to a $121.64 all-time high in January 2026 before correcting to the $84 range. GoldSilver.com argues retail investors focused on price-chasing miss the structural case: six consecutive years of supply deficit, 762 million ounces of cumulative drawdowns, and a gold-to-silver ratio of 55:1 that remains historically elevated — with the real entry framework tied to ratio reversion, not spot price.
